text: [See CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. 1, Coverage A, ¶ 2.d.] Although not necessarily subject to the exclusive remedy provisions of workers' compensation, such claims are considered to arise out of and in the course of employment and thus are covered by workers' compensation. “[I]njuries arising from termination of employment ordinarily arise out of and occur in the course of employment within the meaning of Labor Code section 3600 … [B]oth the act of termination and the acts leading up to termination necessarily arise out of and occur during and in the course of the employment.” [See Shoemaker v. Myers (1990) 52 C3d 1, 19-20, 276 CR 303, 314—dealing with workers' comp insurance] (4) [3:367] Employers' liability exclusion: Injuries arising from employment but not within workers' compensation are also specifically excluded by the employers' liability exclusion (see ¶ 3:315). [See CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. 1, Coverage A, ¶ 2.e.] [3:368 - 3:374] Reserved. b. [3:375] Coverage under separate “personal injury liability” coverage?
